contract: Consumer-Repo PostgreSQL/pgvector exact cosine chunk store: immutable per-index descriptor, atomic serialized source replacement, tenant and allowed-source SQL filtering before bounded distance ranking, non-null provenance and caller-snapshot retrieval candidates for current context-selection recheck; no provider calls or permission decision.
limits: Finite PostgreSQL16/vector scenarios, not proofs; storage/transaction and cosine behavior remain upstream.
Consumer owns Repo/types, installed extension and usable extension-owned type/operator search path, trusted schemas, deployment, credentials and permission snapshots.
No ANN, ranking quality, source authentication, retention/deletion policy, monotonic-version policy, embedding calls or exactly-once guarantee.
Source1..65536 chunks,1MiB each/8MiB total; queryk1..256 and8MiB whole-result bound.
Source-global chunk indices are distinct from batch-local embedding indices; caller owns the association.
Explicit same-process caller transaction refused; raw-BEGIN and Sandbox limits remain as documented.
Extension namespace-unavailability is integration-tested; literal absent pg_extension catalog entry is not.

grounding.claim: S1-S11 finite real PostgreSQL/vector scenarios: real chunker output joined with fixture batch-local embedding records and stored provenance, tenant/permitted-source SQL filtering before ranking, access revocation through context-selection, immutable declaration/descriptor/norm checks, bounds and whole-result refusal, stable ties and identity, real statement timeout and caller transaction refusal, paused replacement with concurrent readers and serialized writers, installed extension unavailable through a restricted Repo search path without shared extension changes; copied-consumer execution. S11 observes actual Repo/Postgrex result content at overflow, exact 8 MiB and one-byte-below boundaries; no universal BEAM heap bound is claimed.
Pgvector0.4.2 float32 encoding, Postgrex extensions and Ecto vector type; server cosine distance is upstream behavior, not locally proved.
Consumer Repo transactions, query connection ownership and query telemetry are upstream contracts.

The consumer supplies authentic frozen-source and embedding association/provenance, trusted database schemas/search path, truthful permission snapshots, and rechecks current access before model injection.

telemetry.contract: Consumer Repo query telemetry can contain SQL parameters; consumer owns handlers/privacy. Elzoo adds no events.

config.contract: Fixed Repo/prefix/index descriptor and1..60000ms statement timeout(default5000); per-call queryk1..256, permitted sources<=256 and1..8MiB content bound may narrow. No hot update.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle; consumer owns Repo and schema deployment.
